new_statements.translation: 3.1.3 Prosodemes. Tone can be called a prosodeme of great importance in the Central Saharan languages. According to Tucker & Bryan tone plays an important, partly phonologically relevant role in these languages. I studied this problem specifically for the vocalic phonemes. The Central Saharan languages perhaps had such a tone system, remnants of which have also been preserved in Berti (Berti [1965] §2.7.2 ff.). About the accent [stress], however, we know only little. Quantity we consider phonologically irrelevant. Here too Berti shares the general Central Saharan traits.

Nach T-B spielt der Ton.. eine wichtige, zum Teil phonologisch relevante Rolle.. dessen Überreste auch im Berti erhalten geblieben sind (B 2.7.2 ff.). Über den Akzent wissen wir allerdings nur wenig. Die Quantität halten wir für phonologisch irrelevant. Auch hier nimmt das Berti an den allgemeinen zentralsaharanischen Zügen teil.' Only differences fr…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No stress rule is given anywhere. The only first-hand analyst of Berti (Petráček, working from Holý's 1961 transcriptions of the last two speakers plus older wordlists) describes Berti prosody as a vestigial tone system (high/low/neutral marks, a tendency for adjacent syllables to differ in tone, a few doubtful tonal minimal pairs such as dō 'smoke' vs dō 'shop') and states explicitly that little is known about accent; vowel quantity is non-phonemic. The 1965 phonology (§2.7, pp. 354-358) has no sentence on Akzent/Betonung at all.
new_statements.exceptions: None; Petráček stresses the unreliability of the material (two c. 80-year-old rememberers, transcription via English/Arabic) and that tone was recorded only by Holý.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern isolated words in wordlists (citation forms); tone patterns tabulated for mono-, di- and trisyllabic nouns (1965 pp. 355-357).
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the same variety: Berti = Siga / Sagato-a ('language of the Saga'), Gebel Tagabo and Duda area, northern Darfur (bert1249, ISO byt). Petráček's data are Holý's 1961 recordings of the last two elderly speakers plus MacMichael (c. 1920), Arkell (ms.) and Spence (1918) wordlists; the language was already effectively extinct, so the description is of rememberers' citation forms.

sources.note: §3.1.3 'Prosodeme', p. 111: tone is the important prosodeme of Central Saharan, remnants of a tone system survive in Berti (referring to 1965 §2.7.2); 'Über den Akzent wissen wir allerdings nur wenig.'; quantity phonologically irrelevant. This is the only explicit sentence about accent in the Berti literature I could open.

sources.note: §2.7 'Prosodische Eigenschaften' (pp. 354-358) treats only vowel quantity (2.7.1: 'keine phonologische Relevanz') and tone (2.7.2-2.7.3: three tone marks in Holý's 1961 transcription, a tendency to alternate tones across syllables, a handful of possible tonal minimal pairs; conclusion p. 358: 'Es ist jedoch wahrscheinlich, daß das Tonalsystem ehemals eine wichtige Rolle in der Prosodie der Bertisprache spielte.. In der fast ausgestorbenen Bertisprache sind nur einige Reste des ehemaligen Systems erhalten geblieben.'). The words Akzent/Betonung/Druck do not occur; no statement on word stress.
